request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Patient Name: [Redacted]

Admission Date: [Redacted]
Discharge Date: [Redacted]
Admitting Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted following diagnosis of mucosal malignant melanoma of the hard palate. The tumor was found to have extensively spread within the hard palate with no involvement of the nasal cavity or nasopharynx, and with no neck lymph node metastasis.

Treatment:
The patient refused surgery and underwent CIR at another facility as the initial treatment, followed by concurrent chemotherapy. After one cycle of chemotherapy was stopped due to severe hematological toxicity. The patient achieved a complete response following CIR and was monitored by physical examinations, endoscopy, enhanced CT, and MRI. At 16 months after CIR, a cervical metastasis of a left jugular lymph node was detected, leading to diagnosis of stage crT0N1M0 MMMHN. The patient was treated by en bloc salvage ND with preservation of the accessory nerve, internal jugular vein, and sternocleidomastoid muscle. The duration of surgery was 132 min, and blood loss was less than 10 mL. The patient was discharged on postoperative Day 7.

Postoperative Management:
The patient experienced no Clavien-Dindo grade 3 or 4 postoperative complications. No recurrence was found by the whole-body enhanced CT performed 3 months after surgery.
Final Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up Care:
Patient will continue to be monitored for any signs of recurrence or metastasis.

Discussions:
The patient was presented with several treatment options, including radiotherapy and systemic immunotherapy, before choosing surgery. The en bloc salvage ND with preservation of the accessory nerve, internal jugular vein, and sternocleidomastoid muscle was performed successfully, and the patient experienced no postoperative complications.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode was for salvage neck dissection for a cervical lymph node metastasis. The primary tumour, a mucosal melanoma of the hard palate, had a complete response after carbon-ion radiotherapy (CIR), so it is no longer present. The condition treated in this admission is the secondary malignant neoplasm of the left jugular lymph node.

ICD-10-AM codes secondary neoplasm of cervical lymph nodes to C77 (secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes), specifically C77.0 for lymph nodes of the head, face and neck.

An alternative would be C43 or C06, with the primary coded as a history of malignancy. Coding rules direct that when a primary malignancy has been eradicated and the admission is for treatment of a metastasis, the secondary site is the principal diagnosis. The primary is then coded as a personal history (Z85), so C77 is the principal diagnosis here.

CODE: C77
